subject: Offer fingerprint + co-sell routing: canonical mapping for AWS/Azure/GCP listings
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Lang <evan@cloudchannel.io>, aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com
Date: Tue, 05 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Offer fingerprint + co-sell routing: canonical mapping for AWS/Azure/GCP listings

Team — starting the thread to lock down a single 'offer fingerprint' that we can export to each cloud's listing template and use as the source of truth for co-sell routing. The goal is to decide: which SKU variants we publish per cloud, which regions to prioritize for initial GA, and the co-sell metadata (tags, entitlements, marketplace categories).

Background: CloudChannel (Evan CC'd) is helping coordinate the three publishers and flagged that inconsistent SKU naming across clouds is delaying co-sell enablement. I put a first pass in the attached spreadsheet with canonical attributes (sku_id, tier, commitment, hourly/reserved, public_regions). Please review the proposal columns: redwood-core-small, redwood-core-large, redwood-dedicated-1yr, redwood-inference-burst.

Proposed quick decisions (we can change after replies):
- AWS: publish fine-grained hourly + 1yr reserved SKUs (us-east-1, us-west-2) so co-sell reps have demonstrable pricing.
- Azure: package by tier (Core/Turbo/Dedicated-1yr) and target East US + West Europe (UK South) first.
- GCP: single region-limited offers for launch (us-central1, europe-west1) with explicit note about GPU family availability.

Ask: Hannah — can you validate the regional capacity constraints for Dedicated SKUs this week? Rafael — can you confirm co-sell tag schema that will be sent to AWS? Evan — any constraints from the partner side on naming conventions we need to adopt?

Thanks,
Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Principal GTM Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
Attachment: 2026-08-05-offer-fingerprint-draft.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
Attachment: marketplace-packaging-guidelines.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Evan Lang <evan@cloudchannel.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com
Date: Tue, 05 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Offer fingerprint + co-sell routing: canonical mapping for AWS/Azure/GCP listings

Marissa — thanks for starting this. Quick notes from the channel side:
- Naming: AWS prefers short SKU identifiers (<=32 chars) without underscores for their listing portal; hyphens are OK. We should supply both a display name and the canonical sku_id.
- Regions: AWS will require that reserved SKUs be limited to regions where we can guarantee reserved capacity inventory; us-east-1 and us-west-2 are safe. For burst/non-reserved we can list a wider footprint, but pricing must be clearly labeled.
- Co-sell tags: we recommend three tags for sales routing: partner-tier (gold|silver), solution-type (inference|embeddings), and commitment (hourly|1yr). We can map these to AWS internal fields.

I reviewed your spreadsheet briefly — see inline comments in the attached (I added a short 'channel_notes' column). Also included: marketplace-packaging-guidelines.pdf from AWS partner docs.

Evan
--
Evan Lang
Director, Channel Integrations — CloudChannel Partners
evan@cloudchannel.io
Attachment: 2026-08-05-offer-fingerprint-draft.xlsx (commented)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Lang <evan@cloudchannel.io>, gcp-partner-success@google.com
Date: Wed, 06 Aug 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Offer fingerprint + co-sell routing: canonical mapping for AWS/Azure/GCP listings

Marissa — looked at the Dedicated SKU capacity plan. A few operational constraints to flag:
- Dedicated-1yr: we can commit capacity in us-east-1 and us-west-2 but need a 30% buffer for trial/demo VMs. If the sales team wants to expose Dedicated-1yr in europe-west1, we need a separate capacity request to infra (lead time 6 weeks).
- Packaging: for Azure, the marketplace listing template forces a single "plan" field per offer. That means the Azure entry should consolidate the hourly and 1yr into distinct plans (e.g., Core-Hourly, Core-1yr) rather than a single SKU with variants.
- GCP: GPU SKU families differ by zone; I recommend that we label GCP offers as "zone-optimized" and include an availability matrix in the listing.

Action items I can take this week: fill in a capacity matrix in the spreadsheet for Dedicated SKUs and call out which regions need infra approval. Rafael — can you prepare the initial co-sell tag mapping to internal AWS fields?

Hannah
--
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Attachment: co-sell-eligibility-checklist.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Lang <evan@cloudchannel.io>, aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com, gcp-partner-success@google.com
Date: Thu, 07 Aug 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Offer fingerprint + co-sell routing: canonical mapping for AWS/Azure/GCP listings

All — summary and decisions after alignment calls this morning: 

1) Canonical offer fingerprint (finalized):
   - sku_id pattern: redwood-{product}-{tier}-{commitment} (hyphenated; max 32 chars where possible)
   - display name: "Redwood Inference — {Tier} ({commitment})"

2) Cloud-specific publishing rules:
   - AWS: expose hourly + 1yr reserved as separate SKUs; initial regions: us-east-1, us-west-2. Tag mapping: partner-tier -> AWS.PartnerTier, solution-type -> AWS.SolutionType, commitment -> AWS.BillingCommitment.
   - Azure: publish as Plans within a single Offer (Core/Turbo/Dedicated-1yr). Regions for GA: East US, UK South. Azure requires consolidated pricing sheets per plan.
   - GCP: publish minimal footprint offers for GA (us-central1, europe-west1) with a required availability matrix for GPU zones. Use a single offer with zone-optimized SKUs.

3) Co-sell enablement steps (owners):
   - Marissa: finalize spreadsheet and push canonical CSV to Channel (due 2026-08-10).
   - Hannah: raise infra request for europe-west1 Dedicated capacity (ticket raised by 2026-08-12).
   - Rafael: push tag mapping to AWS ops and prepare the co-sell enablement doc for internal sales (due 2026-08-11).

Attachments: I attached the finalized fingerprint worksheet and the checklist. Evan — please confirm if channel-side naming constraints are satisfied; if so we'll proceed to publish drafts next week and kick off co-sell enablement.

Thanks — this should get the publishers aligned without rework on each marketplace template.

Rafael
--
Rafael Mendes
Head of GTM Partnerships, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
